entries.title: 2 Chronicles 10:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Grievous - It is probable, when Solomon had declined from God, that God left him to himself to act thus impolitically.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 10:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: If thou be kind, &100. - Moderate counsels are generally best. Gentleness will do what violence will not do. Good words cost nothing but a little self - denial, and yet they purchase great things.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 10:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: See to thine own house - When public affairs are in a ferment, violent proceedings do but make ill worse. Many have been driven to the mischief they did not intend, by being too severely dealt with.
